title: Hastings Castle to get £288,500 from Historic England for repairs
text:
Hastings Borough Council has been awarded £288,500 from Historic England's Heritage at Risk Capital Fund for repairs to Hastings Castle.

The grant, combined with £200,000 from the council, will pay for urgent conservation work, including stabilising vulnerable sections of the curtain walls, conserving the tower wall, chapel arch and Collegiate Church remains, repairing the Ladies' Parlour wall, and addressing vegetation, masonry defects and other vulnerable historic features.

Cllr Julia Hilton, the council's deputy leader and lead councillor for shaping place, regeneration and community wealth building, said the castle was a key part of the town's and the country's heritage, and that the work was needed to protect both the scheduled monument and the public visiting the site.

Louise Brennan, director of regions at Historic England, said the funding would support urgent conservation needs while helping projects move towards sustainable futures.

title: Hastings Philharmonic Choir to sing Schubert and Saint-Saëns
text:
The Hastings Philharmonic Choir's next concert, Songs of Light, brings two choral masterpieces to All Saints Church in the Old Town on Saturday 7 November.

The programme is built around Schubert's Mass in G and Saint-Saëns' Oratorio de Noël, the Christmas Oratorio. The choir will be joined by soloists including Beth Yates and Helen May (sopranos), Kerry Gentleman (contralto), John Twitchen (tenor) and Geoff Williams (baritone), with the strings of the Hastings Philharmonic Orchestra conducted by Marcio da Silva.

Both composers were young when they wrote the works. Schubert, aged 18, composed the Mass in G in six days in March 1815, and Saint-Saëns, 23, finished his oratorio in under two weeks before its first performance in Paris in December 1858.

Tickets range from free to £22.50 and are on sale via the choir's website, The Bookkeeper on Kings Road, St Leonards, and Bookbuster on Queens Road, Hastings.

title: Gruffalo parade to close Hastings Storytelling Festival on the Stade
text:
The Hastings Storytelling Festival comes to a close on Sunday, October 25, with a free Children's Day on the Stade and a Gruffalo themed parade through the Old Town.

Produced by 18 Hours in partnership with the Hastings Storytelling Festival charity, this year's festival, themed Connections, has been running in venues across the town over recent days.

On Sunday, the Stade hosts puppetry, music, walkabout acts and creative workshops, including Pirate Gem's Swashbuckling Adventure show from CBeebies, Long Nose Puppets, Circo Rum Baba's Pesky Pirates and Mermaid Tales on giant seahorses.

Festival patron Axel Scheffler, the illustrator of The Gruffalo, has invited guest author and illustrator Tor Freeman to join the celebrations. A spokesperson for 18 Hours said everyone is welcome to dress up and join the parade, lining up from 2.45pm to parade with local drumming groups and hand painted costumes created by carnival artist Donna Fox.

title: On this day 1823: New town hall market opens in the High Street
text:
On 25 October 1823, the new town hall in the High Street opened its ground floor to the market traders, with 14 stalls taking up their positions.

The foundation stone of the building had been laid just over four months earlier, on 2 June 1823. The market floor offered meat on Wednesdays and Saturdays, and fruit, fish, eggs and the like on other days, with the market closed on Sundays.

As the town's needs changed, the ground floor took on other roles, becoming home to a police station and a fire station. The building is now the Old Town Hall Museum.

title: Hastings and Rye MP criticises Bayeux Tapestry ticket phone system
places: Hastings, St Leonards, Rye, Bexhill, Battle
text:
The MP for Hastings and Rye has criticised the phone line the British Museum set up for local residents to book tickets for the Bayeux tapestry exhibition.

The museum offered people from '1066 Country', the towns with the historic link to the 1066 battle, an early chance to book the latest tranche of tickets from Monday this week, provided they could prove they lived in the area.

But Helena Dollimore, the MP for Hastings and Rye, said constituents were being kept on hold for hours. One person booked after two hours and 38 minutes in the queue, she said, and another was on hold for two and a half hours. She called the system 'glitchy and shambolic' and asked why constituents had to work on a phone line when online booking was clearly possible for others.

A British Museum spokesperson said demand for the exhibition had been 'exceptionally high' and that the offer to residents was on a first-come, first-served basis. All residents remain able to book tickets as part of the general sale on 21 October, and a third tranche of tickets is due to be released in the new year.

title: West Hill Lift gets £531,000 from National Lottery Heritage Fund
text:
The National Lottery Heritage Fund has offered £531,000 in development funding to Hastings Borough Council to secure the long-term future of the West Hill Lift, the Grade II listed lift that runs up the cliff from George Street to Hastings Castle.

The money will pay for the detailed design work and planning consents the council says it needs before making a further bid for funding to fully restore the lift, which requires major work to improve accessibility and reliability.

A council spokesperson indicated the full restoration is likely to cost around £3.8 million, 'but it very much depends on what the development stage shows'.

Cllr Julia Hilton, deputy leader of the council and lead councillor for regeneration, said the future of the lift is 'a vital part' of the Hastings Castle project funded by the Town Deal, and thanked the Heritage Fund and National Lottery players for the grant.

title: Warm Homes Plan cuts would be 'terrible blunder', local energy service warns
text:
A local energy advice service has warned that cuts to the government's Warm Homes Plan would be a 'terrible blunder' for households across East Sussex.

The Hastings Online Times reports the government is set to slash funding for the plan in next week's budget, following a Guardian report that ministers were 'preparing to slash the amount of money available', including hundreds of millions of pounds from the Boiler Upgrade Scheme, which helps households switch from gas boilers to cleaner heating such as heat pumps.

Energise Sussex Coast, which runs a free energy advice service across the county, says the cut would hurt households, the climate and national security. Its director, Kate Meakin, said that in the midst of the current gas crisis it was worse for the government to cut funding for a plan that would reduce Britain's exposure to fossil fuel markets.

The move has also been criticised by the innovation charity Nesta, which said it would 'take the wind out of an industry at a critical stage of development'.

title: Hastings artist to launch book of paintings made through cancer
text:
Hastings artist Helen Slater will launch her book Uninvited on the afternoon of Sunday 25 October, hosted by The Peripheral Space Project.

Ms Slater, who works in acrylic, began painting on 31 July, the day she was told she had breast cancer. Colour, texture and abstract form became a way to express what she described as a cascade of words no one expected to hear: tumour, scans, hormone blockers, operation.

She kept creating throughout her experience, producing 21 paintings and a short diary that began as private acts of processing and calm. They were first shared at The Peripheral Space in November 2025, an event where the idea for the book was born.

Uninvited gathers the work into an illustrated collection exploring fear, vulnerability, hope, resilience and gratitude. Erica Smith, who worked with Helen on the design of the book, calls it 'a remarkable combination of words and her paintings'.
